summary: Subtle top-k drift after mixed float64->fp32 coercion in embedding ingestion pipeline
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a reproducible, low-amplitude drift in rerank order for an enterprise production workflow after a bulk re-ingest. Impact: Top-5 ordering for rerank lists changes subtly across >1% of queries, causing downstream UX tests to fail non-deterministically. Degradation is not a full outage but causes incorrect search ranking for high-precision use cases (medical records).
steps_to_reproduce: Customer uploads a batch of embeddings produced by a local numpy pipeline (float64) followed by a smaller batch produced by a PyTorch pipeline (float32) using the same namespace/namespace-version.
Both batches are uploaded to the embeddings API via multipart parallel workers that use the standard SDK with automatic dtype inference.
After ingestion completes, customer runs their rerank job that queries top-k similarity against the combined shard set.
Observe top-5 differences between runs when the two batch orders are flipped (float64-first vs float32-first).

comments: Priya Sharma (Support): Customer reports 1-2% top-5 reordering after a scheduled re-ingest yesterday. They provided sample query IDs and a small payload reproducer. Asked for ingestion metadata and SDK versions.

Diego Morales (Eng): Confirmed logs show automated downcast to fp32 during write. Need to determine whether the coercion is performed deterministically and whether it changes vector rounding behavior. Assigning to embeddings infra to verify storage serialization path.

SRE (Investigation): Found that the ingest pipeline has a heuristics branch that coerces float64->float32 when batch_size > 1024 to save space. This was introduced in commit github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-service@b4a9c3 (storage-precision-heuristic).

Customer (MediTech): Provided two sample query IDs (Q-1001, Q-1002) and said the ordering flip affects triage for priority cases. Asked if a rollback or re-ingest is possible and how to avoid the issue in the future.

Diego Morales (Eng): Suggested a targeted re-ingest of the smaller float32 batch into a new namespace to compare behavior. Also requested embedded sample vectors from customer to run local similarity checks.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Non-deterministic rounding introduced by float64->float32 coercion at the ingest path changes the last 1-2 decimal places of certain vector components, enough to change tie-breakers in dense similarity top-k for near neighbors.

Reproduction: Using customer's sample payloads, a local reranker run shows top-5 differences when coercion is applied vs. when original float64 vectors are preserved and compared using float64 similarity computation. The magnitude of cosine delta is ~1.2e-6 on average for affected pairs but sufficient to flip ordering in tightly clustered results.

Root cause candidate: storage-precision-heuristic in ingest-service downcasts float64 inputs to fp32 without preserving a header indicating original dtype; downstream reranker always treats stored vectors as fp32 which silently changes similarity calculations, especially for near-duplicate items.
Related: No explicit dtype header persisted with batch metadata in v1 of the namespace. There is an open PR to add dtype metadata (see related_github_prs).
Risk assessment: High for high-precision customers (medical/legal). Low for standard consumer workloads. Non-urgent for availability but urgent for correctness for this customer.
resolution: Pending: mitigation path identified. Short-term workaround is to re-ingest float64-produced batches into a separate namespace that preserves float64 or to enable 'preserve_dtype' flag in a forthcoming ingest-service patch. Engineering has a PR to add explicit dtype metadata and to disable the heuristic when customer_tier=enterprise (PR referenced). SRE will schedule a targeted re-ingest support window with the customer after approval.
next_steps: Eng to merge PR that adds explicit dtype metadata and an opt-out for the auto-downcast heuristic (target: 2026-03-18).
Support to coordinate a controlled re-ingest with MediTech for a 1-hour maintenance window and validate rerank ordering post-reingest.
Add a telemetry alert for 'dtype_coercion_count' > 0 for enterprise namespaces to surface to Console and support channels.
Document guidance in KB: 'Avoid mixed-dtype bulk-ingests in same namespace' and add recommended CLI flags.
